body:
## Pull request overview

This pull request refactors the ObjectUI CLI from a standalone Commander.js-based tool (`@object-ui/cli`) into an oclif plugin (`@objectstack/plugin-ui`), enabling integration with the unified ObjectStack CLI ecosystem while maintaining backward compatibility.

**Changes:**
- Migrated all 15 CLI commands to oclif Command classes under `src/commands/ui/` directory
- Added `@oclif/core` dependency and oclif plugin configuration to `package.json`
- Split `tsup.config.ts` into two build passes: library entries with TypeScript definitions and oclif commands as runtime-only builds
- Created comprehensive test coverage with 55 tests validating all oclif command classes
- Added migration documentation (`MIGRATION.md`) and updated README and ROADMAP
- Fixed pre-existing issues: unused `req` parameter renamed to `_req`, `@ts-expect-error` changed to `@ts-ignore`

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 24 out of 25 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| pnpm-lock.yaml | Added @oclif/core and dependencies; removed hotcrm example entries (⚠️ potentially unintended) |
| packages/cli/tsup.config.ts | Split build config into lib entries (with DTS) and oclif commands (runtime-only) |
| packages/cli/package.json | Renamed to @objectstack/plugin-ui, added oclif config and vitest |
| packages/cli/src/index.ts | Updated header comment, added comment for programmatic exports |
| packages/cli/src/commands/ui/*.ts | 15 new oclif Command classes wrapping original command functions |
| packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts | Changed @ts-expect-error to @ts-ignore for lucidePath assignment |
| packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts | Renamed unused `req` parameter to `_req` |
| packages/cli/src/__tests__/oclif-commands.test.ts | New test suite with 55 tests for oclif command structure |
| packages/cli/README.md | Updated for new package name and installation instructions |
| packages/cli/MIGRATION.md | New comprehensive migration guide with command mappings and deprecation timeline |
| ROADMAP.md | Updated CLI command counts and architecture notes |
</details>


<details>
<summary>Files not reviewed (1)</summary>

* **pnpm-lock.yaml**: Language not supported
</details>
This arg description contains Chinese text, which violates the English-only codebase rule (Rule #-1). All user-facing text must be in English. Consider using only "Application name".

This flag description contains Chinese text, which violates the English-only codebase rule (Rule #-1). All user-facing text must be in English. Consider using only "Template to use (dashboard, form, simple)".

The imports `Args` and `Flags` from '@oclif/core' are unused in this test file. They should be removed to keep the imports clean.
```suggestion
import { Command } from '@oclif/core';
```

The migration documentation shows the new command as `os ui create-plugin <name>`, but the original Commander.js command was `objectui create plugin <name>` (with a space between 'create' and 'plugin'). This is a breaking change in command structure that should be more prominently highlighted in the migration guide. Consider adding this to the "Flag Changes" table or creating a new "Command Structure Changes" section to clearly document that users need to change from `objectui create plugin <name>` to `os ui create-plugin <name>` (hyphenated).

The pnpm-lock.yaml shows removal of all hotcrm example package dependencies (lines 576-845 in the original), but the hotcrm directory still exists in the examples folder. This appears to be an unintended side effect of the PR changes and could cause dependency resolution issues. The hotcrm packages should either be retained in the lockfile if they're still in use, or the removal should be documented as an intentional cleanup in the PR description.

This description contains Chinese text, which violates the English-only codebase rule (Rule #-1). According to the architectural guidelines, all user-facing text in components, documentation, comments, and UI labels must be written in English. While this text was present in the original Commander.js code, the migration provides an opportunity to clean this up. Consider using only the English portion: "Initialize a new Object UI application with sample schema".
